title.en: Spectacular Wonders: mysteries of nature in India

text.en: India has natural wonders that surprise and spark our imagination. Have you seen a bridge made from living roots?

India is home to many mystifying natural phenomena, which are strange and hard to explain.
The Valley of Flowers in Uttarakhand is an eye-catching spectacle with around 600 species of flowers.
In Meghalaya, bamboo and wooden bridges did not last in heavy rains, so local people grew living root bridges from intertwined roots.
A root bridge is a naturally built ecosystem and can last for centuries under ideal conditions.
These bridges show the knowledge and bond that the indigenous people have with their land.
The Lonar Crater Lake in Buldhana district, Maharashtra, is a geological wonder, a giant hole believed to be formed thousands of years ago.
A report on wonders is informative text: it gives facts, names places and describes features.
Vocabulary: spectacle is an unusual sight, futile is useless, nestled is sheltered, and persist is to continue.
We should protect these wonders because they are a part of our natural heritage.

problem.en: Why are living root bridges a good idea?

text.en: Wood and bamboo bridges rot in heavy rain.
Roots keep growing and get stronger.
They are made from local plants and last for centuries.
